deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics, and it is not in Riemann's hand. It is the closing page of a letter by H. A. Schwarz, signed 'H. A. Schwarz, Weender Chaussée 25A' (Göttingen). The date '18 Jan. 76' on the preceding page places it in January 1876. The letter was evidently filed with the Riemann Nachlass bundle on minimal surfaces.

Content, paraphrased: Schwarz regrets that the letter is unpleasant news. He is sure the addressee will be annoyed that the trust and great forbearance shown to Herr Hattendorf have been so poorly repaid. Had Schwarz been able to see Hattendorf's manuscript beforehand, most of the passages he objects to could perhaps have been replaced by more carefully chosen ones. Now the addressee faces an awkward choice. He must either urge the publisher (Verlagsbuchhändler) to accept larger changes, or keep the serious defects. Even the indispensable changes cannot be settled in a hurry. Schwarz complains that Hattendorf took the earlier lesson so little to heart. At least sending him the proof sheet (Correcturbogen) has had the benefit that the errors were noticed. He hopes the addressee will not hold a grudge against him for having the misfortune to find so many mistakes. He then sends personal greetings, asks after the addressee's wife and children, and offers New Year wishes.

Context: the previous page is the end of Schwarz's technical critique of K. Hattendorf's edition of Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung'. That critique concerns the counting of real constants in the Riemann–Weierstrass representation and the superfluous equations (13) and (16). The proof sheets are presumably those of the 1876 edition of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke. The question about a wife and children fits Heinrich Weber, the chief editor; Dedekind was unmarried. This identification of the addressee is an inference, not stated on the page.

No derivation is present to reconstruct.
